covers.quote: Use symbols for common units of measurement
You don’t need to spell out units of measurement, even for the first use, if they’re well known and users will know what they mean.

examples.note: First use spelled out with symbol in parentheses; subsequent use uses symbol.

parts.quote: The noise from the building site was 120 decibels (dB). Workers in the nearby office preferred a limit of only 50 dB.

rules.quote: Spell out units of measurement the first time you use them if users won’t immediately understand them. After that, use the symbols.
rules.specification: Common units (mm, cm, km, km/h) need not be spelled out. Other units should be spelled out at first mention with their symbol in parentheses, and the symbol used thereafter.
rules.violation_condition: a unit of measurement that is unfamiliar or uncommon introduced without being spelled out on first use, or spelled out continuously after being introduced
when: Units of measurement are used that target audiences will not immediately understand.
Well-known units (e.g. mm, cm, km, km/h) do not need to be spelled out on first use.
rules.why: G-2, G-3, G-4: Merges general abbreviation convention with permission for common units.

parts.quote: Queensland is 1,853 million km2 in area.
Queensland is 1,853 million square km in area.

rules.quote: Don’t combine symbols and words for units.
rules.violation_condition: mixing spelled-out words and unit symbols in a single compound measurement expression
rules.why: Clear standalone prohibition on hybrid unit expressions.

parts.quote: There was 5 μg of active ingredient in each capsule.
There was 5 mcg of active ingredient in each capsule.
He measured 50 mL of water.
He measured 5 dL of water.

rules.violation_condition: use of non-standard unit symbols or prefixes (e.g. 'mcg' instead of 'µg', or 'dL' instead of standard units)
rules.why: Clear standalone prohibition supported by contrast examples.

rules.quote: Days, years, hours and minutes measure time. These are not SI units. Spell them out in full – unless they’re in a table, list or chart and are easy to understand.

when: Referring to time quantities (days, years, hours, minutes).
Does not apply in tables, lists, or charts where abbreviations are easy to understand.

rules.quote: use a non-breaking space between numbers and their units of measurement.
rules.specification: Use a non-breaking space (  / U+00A0) between a numeral and unit symbol or word, except where established industry conventions omit the space (e.g. 750mL wine bottles).

when: A number is written with a unit of measurement.
Industry-specific applications may omit the space by convention.
rules.why: G-4: Consolidates repeated instructions across the page regarding non-breaking spaces between numbers and units.

rules.quote:
Make it easy for users to compare quantities. Use the same:
[33f3bfb24095] LI  unit and prefix
[aea00166fe03] LI  number of decimal places.
rules.specification: When presenting multiple measurements of the same item or in comparison, ensure they use the identical unit/prefix and consistent decimal precision.
rules.violation_condition: measurements being compared in the same context that use inconsistent units, prefixes, or decimal places
when: Comparing measurements in the same sentence or immediate context.
rules.why: G-4: Rule consolidated from heading and list instruction with comparative examples.

rules.quote: Most government content should use ‘L’ as it’s clearer to users (‘l’ can be confused with ‘I’ and ‘1’).

rules.why: Specific preference rule for litre symbol casing.

covers.quote: Avoid imperial units

rules.quote: Don’t use imperial units of measurement in Australia unless you have a specific reason
rules.specification: Avoid imperial units (gallons, barrels, inches, feet, miles) unless in historical quotes or writing for countries using imperial measures. Provide SI equivalents where used.

when: Exceptions: historical quotations, or content specifically for international audiences where imperial measures apply.
rules.why: G-2, G-4: Rule on imperial units combined with its exceptions and advice to provide SI equivalents.
